To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
India's HIV/AIDS epidemic is complex, with a high prevalence in certain groups and geographic areas, and that India's response has been successful in controlling the epidemic.
India's response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic is based on a well-organised, comprehensive and integrated system of data collection and analysis.

India is an example where ‘know your epidemic’ and ‘know your response’ have been implemented at scale and that this experience offers important lessons to help others design their evidence generation system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) What is the nature of data sources and their utility for understanding the HIV epidemic in India?;
the use of data for evidence-based decision making in the context of HIV/AIDS, and the role of data systems and data use in the evolution of the Indian response to the epidemic.
how the HIV epidemic in India has been understood, the evolution of data systems and how they have contributed to the design and implementation of a national response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIV/AIDS epidemic in India is now well understood, and the national response has been well tailored to address the specific needs of the country.
the data generated and used for HIV/AIDS in India have been a key enabler of the country's effective and efficient HIV response.

India has made great strides in the generation, analysis and utilisation of HIV data for an effective AIDS response and that these efforts have been instrumental in reducing HIV incidence in the country and in saving millions of lives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to know our epidemic, know our responses and know our data systems.
India has developed a robust system of data generation, collection, analysis and use to guide an effective response to HIV/AIDS.
the data systems and the response to HIV/AIDS in India have evolved in tandem and have become more effective over time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Indian example shows the value of investing in data collection and analysis to inform an effective response to the HIV and AIDS epidemic.
India has been able to generate and use data to inform the HIV epidemic response.
India has made great strides in generating and analysing HIV data and has used these data to inform its AIDS response.
